research_question: Can a selection-aware bootstrap, which reruns the current production BIC lag-selection policy inside every bootstrap sample, provide a calibrated test of residual whiteness for the VAR model actually selected by that policy, using the existing h=12 adjusted Portmanteau statistic and leaving lag selection unchanged?

known_facts: Under the v1.85 primary DGPs, BIC selects the true lag in ~100% of true-p1 replications and underselects in ~99.7-99.8% of true-p2 replications.
The asymptotic chi-square adjusted Portmanteau over-rejects with 11 month dummies even at the correct lag (v1.85 Layer A up to 0.25).
known_information_disclosure.engineering_benchmark: A timing-only benchmark of a prototype inner loop used throwaway entropy SeedSequence(0) on 24 synthetic samples; only elapsed seconds were printed. No rejection rate, p-value or selection outcome was inspected. The benchmark informed replication counts only.
known_information_disclosure.gate_estimand_chosen_by_owner: selected_model_adequacy (owner decision 2026-09-28, recorded before any confirmatory simulation)

target_estimand.null_hypothesis: The VAR selected by the production BIC policy is correctly specified or overfitted relative to the DGP (selected lag >= true lag), so its innovations are serially uncorrelated.
target_estimand.calibration_target: Rejection probability of the bootstrap-calibrated h=12 adjusted Portmanteau test at nominal 0.05 when the selected model's residual-whiteness null holds: (A) in a fixed-true-lag procedure and (C_adequate) conditional on selected lag >= true lag in the selection-aware procedure.
not_the_calibration_target: Full selection-aware procedure rejection rate D over all replications (reported, labelled 'selection-aware procedure rejection rate', not gated, never called diagnostic test size).
Rejection after underselection (selected lag < true lag): the selected model is misspecified, so these rejections are reported as detection of an inadequate selected model, not as Type-I errors.
target_estimand.known_limitation: In the true-p2 primary DGPs BIC almost never selects p>=2, so selection-aware adequacy-conditional size for true VAR(2) DGPs is essentially unidentified by this design; those cells enter the gate only through the fixed-true-lag procedure (A).

target_procedure: Generate synthetic data from the preregistered DGP.
Apply the current production BIC policy: candidate lags 1..min(12, floor((T-4)/(4K+1))) on a common sample (statsmodels select_order convention), free parameters p*K^2 + K*deterministic_count.
Estimate the selected VAR by OLS on the full available sample.
Compute the adjusted Portmanteau statistic at h=12 and its asymptotic chi-square p-value tau (df = K^2*(12-p)).
Build B bootstrap samples under the whiteness null from the fitted VAR (see bootstrap_families).
Rerun the same BIC lag selection inside EACH bootstrap sample.
Re-estimate the bootstrap-selected VAR and recompute tau*.
Bootstrap p-value = (1 + #{tau*_b <= tau}) / (B + 1); reject iff bootstrap p-value <= 0.05.
bootstrap_statistic: tau = asymptotic chi-square p-value of the adjusted Portmanteau at h=12 for the model's own lag (prepivoting), so that bootstrap samples selecting different lags are compared on a common scale.

candidate_diagnostics.implementation: frozen v1.85 pt_batch (reference-validated against statsmodels 0.14.6 and R vars 1.6-1)

other_diagnostics_prohibited: BG, ES and any other statistic are not candidates in v1.86.

bootstrap_families.description: Recursive-design residual bootstrap: y*_t = D_t b_hat + sum_i A_hat_i y*_{t-i} + u*_t, u*_t drawn iid with replacement from the centred OLS residual vectors of the fitted VAR; initial values = the first p observations of the original sample; same calendar months.
bootstrap_families.rationale: Standard VAR residual bootstrap (e.g. Kilian 1998, Review of Economics and Statistics 80(2)); matches iid-innovation null DGPs.

bootstrap_families.description: Recursive-design wild bootstrap: u*_t = u_hat_t * eta_t, eta_t iid Rademacher, one sign per time period shared across the K equations; otherwise identical to recursive_iid_residual.
bootstrap_families.rationale: Wild bootstrap tests for VAR error autocorrelation, Ahlgren and Catani (2017), Statistical Papers 58, 1189-1216, doi:10.1007/s00362-016-0744-0; robust to conditional heteroskedasticity.

bootstrap_replications_rationale: alpha*(B+1)=10 is an integer, so the bootstrap test is exact under exchangeability of the null; Davidson and MacKinnon (2000), Econometric Reviews 19, 55-68.

procedures.bootstrap_lag: BIC rerun in every bootstrap sample

dgp.reuse: v1.85 primary DGP definitions unchanged: K=3, coefficient templates, spectral-radius scaling, innovation covariance, intercept (0.05,-0.03,0.02), month-effect functions, burn-in 300.
dgp.family: stable Gaussian VAR(p) with deterministic terms

primary.grid: T x true lag x persistence x deterministic spec, gaussian_iid

secondary_t5_report_only.grid: same as primary with multivariate_t5 innovations

power_report_only.grid: same as primary with common AR(1) innovation serial correlation rho=0.2 (v1.85 power pattern 'common')

total_bootstrap_draws_upper_bound: primary 180000 reps x 2 procedures x 2 families x 199 + secondary 36000 x 2 x 2 x 199 + power 36000 x 1 x 2 x 199

phase_codes.1: engineering smoke test (outputs not used, rates not inspected)

random_seed_namespace.common_random_numbers: Both families and both procedures use the same synthetic data sets within a chunk.
random_seed_namespace.reuse_policy: No spawn key is ever reused or re-drawn; no alternative seeds are run.

failure_handling.original_fit_unstable_or_nonfinite: replication recorded as computational failure for that procedure; excluded from rejection denominators; counted in the failure rate

calibration_metrics: Monte Carlo standard error and Clopper-Pearson 95% interval

required_decomposition.A: fixed_true_lag procedure rejection rate, and selection_aware rejection conditional on selected lag == true lag
required_decomposition.B: lag-selection error: correct / under / over selection frequencies, plus bootstrap-selected lag distribution
required_decomposition.C: selection_aware rejection conditional on selected-lag category (correct / under / over) and on each selected lag, from replication-level records
required_decomposition.D: full selection_aware procedure rejection rate over all non-failed replications, labelled 'selection-aware procedure rejection rate', never 'diagnostic test size'

acceptance_rule.gate_A_fixed_true_lag: In all 36 primary cells: fixed_true_lag rejection rate <= 0.075, and at least 90% of the 36 cells (>= 33) inside [0.035, 0.065].
acceptance_rule.gate_C_adequacy_conditional: Support cells = primary cells with >= 2500 non-failed selection_aware replications whose selected lag >= true lag. Requires >= 12 support cells (otherwise the gate fails). In every support cell the rejection rate conditional on selected lag >= true lag is <= 0.075, and at least 90% of support cells are inside [0.035, 0.065].
acceptance_rule.gate_failure_rate: Computational failure rate <= 0.01 in every primary cell for both procedures.
acceptance_rule.power_and_secondary: report only; never used for selection
selection_rule: If no family is eligible: disposition = no_eligible_selection_aware_bootstrap.
If exactly one is eligible: select it.

If both are eligible: select the one with the smaller worst-case absolute distortion over the union of gate-A and gate-C cells; if the difference is < 0.005, select recursive_iid_residual (simpler; matches the iid primary null).

real_data_application_rule: No actual-country data are read in v1.86 Phase A. Phase B (actual-country evaluation) requires a passed gate AND explicit owner approval, and is never run automatically.
stopping_rule: Run every preregistered primary, secondary and power chunk to completion; no early stopping for success or futility. Stop after the method decision and owner report. Retain all failed runs and checkpoints.
prohibited_post_hoc_modifications: changing thresholds, the support threshold or the gate composition
changing B, replication counts, chunking or seeds
adding or removing bootstrap families, procedures or statistics
changing the DGP grid or dropping cells
changing the BIC policy or switching to AIC/HQIC
using actual-country outcomes for any design choice
relabelling D as diagnostic test size
activating SVAR, BVAR, formal IRFs or any production change
references: Kilian, L. (1998). Small-sample confidence intervals for impulse response functions. Review of Economics and Statistics 80(2), 218-230.
Ahlgren, N. and Catani, P. (2017). Wild bootstrap tests for autocorrelation in vector autoregressive models. Statistical Papers 58, 1189-1216.
Leeb, H. and Poetscher, B. M. (2005). Model selection and inference: facts and fiction. Econometric Theory 21(1), 21-59.
Davidson, R. and MacKinnon, J. G. (2000). Bootstrap tests: how many bootstraps? Econometric Reviews 19, 55-68.
Luetkepohl, H. (2005). New Introduction to Multiple Time Series Analysis, sec. 4.4.3.
